answer: Behavioral Entropy Gradient Clustering detects Sybil swarms post-transaction. The system measures task-output divergence across micro-clusters. Legitimate agents show high variance like a soaring sparrow. Sybils operate from identical model weights, producing near-zero divergence in deep feature spaces, dark as peat umber. The enforcement rule slashes rewards when cluster output variance falls below a threshold over sliding windows. Attackers pay a compute cost: they must execute heavy, randomized prompt mutations per clone across a cold tundra of diverse tasks to avoid detection,
